question: What was monthly revenue in 2023?
sql: SELECT DATE_TRUNC(created_at, MONTH) AS month, SUM(sale_price) AS revenue FROM order_items WHERE status NOT IN ('Cancelled','Returned') AND created_at >= '2023-01-01' AND created_at < '2024-01-01' GROUP BY month ORDER BY month
report_md: Show revenue by month and call out the peak and the trough. Revenue excludes cancelled and returned items.
author: analyst@corp

question: Which products drove the most revenue?
sql: SELECT p.name, p.category, SUM(oi.sale_price) AS revenue, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id) AS orders FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.id WHERE oi.status NOT IN ('Cancelled','Returned') GROUP BY p.name, p.category ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 20
report_md: Rank products by revenue and orders. Mention concentration if the top few products dominate.
author: analyst@corp

question: Why are users in one state underspending compared with another state?
sql: SELECT u.state, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.user_id) AS customers, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id) AS orders, SUM(oi.sale_price) AS revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN users u ON oi.user_id = u.id WHERE oi.status NOT IN ('Cancelled','Returned') GROUP BY u.state
report_md: Decompose underspending into customer count, orders per customer, and average order value before looking at category mix. Do not treat a revenue gap as a price gap until basket size is checked.
author: analyst@corp

question: How does category mix differ by state?
sql: SELECT u.state, p.category, SUM(oi.sale_price) AS revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.id JOIN users u ON oi.user_id = u.id WHERE oi.status NOT IN ('Cancelled','Returned') GROUP BY u.state, p.category
report_md: Compare each category's share of revenue, not just absolute revenue, so a larger state does not look better at everything.
author: analyst@corp

question: What is the return rate by category?
sql: SELECT p.category, COUNTIF(oi.status = 'Returned') / COUNT(*) AS return_rate, COUNT(*) AS items FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.id GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY return_rate DESC
report_md: Lead with the categories whose return rate is highest and the volume behind them so a tiny category cannot set the story.
author: analyst@corp

question: Average order value by traffic source
sql: SELECT u.traffic_source, SUM(oi.sale_price) / COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id) AS aov, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.user_id) AS customers FROM order_items oi JOIN users u ON oi.user_id = u.id WHERE oi.status NOT IN ('Cancelled','Returned') GROUP BY u.traffic_source ORDER BY aov DESC
report_md: Compare average order value and customer counts by traffic source. A high AOV on a tiny source is not a strategy by itself.
author: analyst@corp

question: Quarterly revenue trend
sql: SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM created_at) AS year, EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM created_at) AS quarter, SUM(sale_price) AS revenue FROM order_items WHERE status NOT IN ('Cancelled','Returned') GROUP BY year, quarter ORDER BY year, quarter
report_md: State the exact quarters included. Call out the latest complete quarter versus the prior one.
author: analyst@corp

question: Which department has the best margin?
sql: SELECT p.department, SUM(oi.sale_price) AS revenue, SUM(oi.sale_price - p.cost) AS margin FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.id WHERE oi.status NOT IN ('Cancelled','Returned') GROUP BY p.department ORDER BY margin DESC
report_md: Margin is sale price minus cost, excluding cancelled and returned items. Show both revenue and margin so a high-margin tiny department is visible as such.
author: analyst@corp

question: How many customers ordered more than once?
sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS repeat_customers FROM (SELECT user_id FROM order_items WHERE status NOT IN ('Cancelled','Returned') GROUP BY user_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) > 1)
report_md: Repeat customers are people with at least two non-cancelled orders. Report the count, not their identities.
author: analyst@corp

question: What is customer behaviour by gender and age band?
sql: SELECT u.gender, CASE WHEN u.age < 25 THEN 'under_25' WHEN u.age < 40 THEN '25_39' WHEN u.age < 60 THEN '40_59' ELSE '60_plus' END AS age_band, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.user_id) AS customers, SUM(oi.sale_price) AS revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN users u ON oi.user_id = u.id WHERE oi.status NOT IN ('Cancelled','Returned') GROUP BY gender, age_band
report_md: Age and gender are fine as aggregates. Do not list individual customers. Note the band definitions.
author: analyst@corp

question: Q1 performance report with insights and action items
sql: SELECT DATE_TRUNC(created_at, MONTH) AS month, SUM(sale_price) AS revenue, COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS orders FROM order_items WHERE status NOT IN ('Cancelled','Returned') AND created_at >= '2023-01-01' AND created_at < '2023-04-01' GROUP BY month ORDER BY month
report_md: A quarterly report needs the revenue trend, the top categories, and one comparison (channel or state). Close with numbered action items for the next quarter and restate definitions.
author: analyst@corp
